clue.text: Finest in Guardian? Crossword answer is here …

definitions.text: Finest in Guardian? Crossword answer is here …

indicators.note: the clue announces that the solution sits inside the preceding words, which is exactly what a hidden word does

parts.note: the letters of the answer run through the first two words, finest and in

explanation.surface: A boast that the best puzzle in a rival newspaper is right here, leading into the riddle that follows.
explanation.walkthrough: The word sits in the letters of Finest in, and the answer itself names the device: a word lodged inside other words is nesting there.
explanation.definitionFit: Nesting means lodging snugly inside something, which is precisely the position of a hidden answer within its clue.

clue.text: Really rather good oil-steeped food, rating alongside

indicators.note: the oil is soaked into the food, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: nosh is informal British slang for food
otto, also called attar, is a fragrant oil pressed from roses
a rating is a non-commissioned sailor, and AB is an able seaman
by means beside or next to

explanation.surface: A grudging verdict on some greasy dish, with its score placed next to it.
explanation.walkthrough: Otto is a rose oil, more often spelt attar; nosh is British slang for grub.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is understated praise, an idiom meaning quite good indeed, which matches really rather good.

clue.text: See 1
Architect is supporting currents run from the ground

indicators.note: in a down answer the piece that supports another sits underneath it

parts.note: two currents: in, meaning fashionable or current, and I, the physics symbol for electric current

indicators.note: read upwards from the bottom, as a down entry climbing off the ground

parts.note: to jog is to run at a gentle pace
read as I's, the plural of the numeral I, which is ones

explanation.surface: An architect's remark about electrical currents running up out of the ground beneath a building.
explanation.walkthrough: The trick is reading is as the plural of I, a Roman one, giving ones. Inigo Jones was the 17th-century English architect of the Banqueting House in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Inigo Jones is a famous English architect, so the answer is an example of the category named.

clue.text: Was opening grand do on roof of Dorchester

parts.note: G is slang for a grand, a thousand pounds or dollars
to do someone is to imitate them, as to ape is

indicators.note: the top of a down entry is its first letter, so this takes the opening letter

parts.note: its first letter, the roof of the word

explanation.surface: Someone launched a lavish party on top of the Dorchester, the luxury London hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: Grand do looks like a party at the Dorchester, a London hotel; here grand gives G and do means imitate.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that gaped was wide open, so gaped is the past tense of being agape or open.

clue.text: … riddle to solve now: in order to do so … "Aha!"

definitions.note: the answer is the opening of an old joke question

indicators.note: solving here means working the letters out into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The setter urges the solver to crack the riddle at once, ending with a triumphant cry of discovery.
explanation.walkthrough: The traditional reply is when it is ajar, a pun on a jar.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the first half of a well-known joke question, so it is a riddle in its own right.

clue.text: Wandering pets?

definitions.meaning: the definition: a long ramble on foot
read as an instruction, the word step walked about, turned round, spells pets

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a reversal joke: pets is step turned round, so it is a step that has walked about.
explanation.definitionFit: A walkabout is a journey on foot with no fixed route, so it is a wandering expedition.

clue.text: Go under the point of the blade

indicators.note: in a down answer, the piece that comes under another is written after it

parts.note: a compass point, here east
to go is a euphemism for urinating, as is to pee

explanation.surface: An instruction to slip in beneath the sharp tip of a sword.
explanation.walkthrough: Go is the polite euphemism for using the toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: An epee is a type of fencing sword, so blade names it by its kind.

clue.text: Ready party to set about hosts

indicators.note: one phrase is placed around the other, enclosing it

parts.note: to be in on something is to be party to it
seas of things, like hosts of them, are vast numbers

explanation.surface: Someone is all set to throw a party for the people hosting them.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit or game that is in season is available and ripe, so ready is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Coat of arms device run down in one family

indicators.note: the moved device goes inside the word for one

parts.note: any is used for one, as in any one of them

indicators.note: the run letter goes down from its place to the bottom of the device in this down entry

parts.note: a crest is the emblem set above the shield in a coat of arms
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A heraldic emblem that has been passed down through one family.
explanation.walkthrough: The R of crest is not lost but moved to the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancestry is the line of descent from which a person comes, so it means family in that lineage sense.

clue.text: A hint of lemon in Asian (specifically Indian) meal

indicators.note: the hint of lemon is placed inside the nationality

parts.note: a Thai is someone from Thailand, an Asian country

indicators.note: a hint is just the first trace, so only the opening letter is taken

parts.note: its first letter is the hint

explanation.surface: A squeeze of lemon added to an Asian dish, which turns out to be Indian.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket is a fair warning: the dish is Indian even though Asian supplies the Thai.
explanation.definitionFit: A thali is an Indian meal served as several small dishes on one round platter.

clue.text: Blooming chamber politician means to focus on bill

parts.note: pol is informal for a politician
a lens is the device that brings light to a focus
AC is short for account, which is a bill

explanation.surface: A politician concentrating on a piece of legislation in a heated debating chamber.
explanation.walkthrough: Blooming looks like a mild British oath on the chamber; it is literal, meaning flowering.
explanation.definitionFit: A pollen sac is the part of a flower's anther that holds pollen, a chamber within a bloom.

clue.text: Using a minor route, Trump's really enjoying a run in Manhattan

parts.note: on as in running on gas, meaning using
a B road is a British minor road, below an A road
way is American slang for really, as in way better, so it is Trump's word

explanation.surface: A tale of a former US president taking back roads and loving a jog through Manhattan.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, B roads are minor routes. Run here is a theatrical run, not a jog.
explanation.definitionFit: A show on Broadway is playing in the theatre district of Manhattan, so it is enjoying a run there.

clue.text: Deep sea resident

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the ..., a fish living in the sea

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a single deep-sea creature, but deep is a separate meaning about sound.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes the lowest musical register and also names a familiar sea fish.

clue.text: Getting sausage from the oven European student drops posh joint

indicators.note: drops says those two letters fall from their place to the bottom of this down answer

parts.note: a saveloy is a highly seasoned smoked sausage
food fresh from the oven is hot
E for European and L for learner, a student driver

explanation.surface: A diner grabbing a sausage hot from the oven while a European student slips off to a smart venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting' and 'from the oven' make it sound like baking, but the student is L, a learner driver; the Savoy is a grand London hotel and a saveloy a British sausage.
explanation.definitionFit: The Savoy is a famous luxury hotel on the Strand, and joint is slang for any establishment.

clue.text: See 5
Engineer gets out of overhauling retrogressive store …

indicators.note: one set of letters is taken out of the other

parts.note: the letters of retrogressive overhauled, that is rearranged, into the store plus the four letters to be removed
gets engineered, its letters rearranged, is still just those four letters

explanation.surface: An engineer leaves after renovating a backward-looking shop.
explanation.walkthrough: The four letters of gets are removed in whatever order they appear before the rest is shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: A reservoir is a store of water, or figuratively any supply held in reserve.

clue.text: … and again Number Two doubled power losses

indicators.note: the second letter, a Roman fifty, is doubled in value to a Roman hundred

parts.note: the dots that end the previous clue, appearing once more here, make two ellipses

explanation.surface: A deputy repeats himself as the power keeps failing.
explanation.walkthrough: The trailing dots on 15 and leading dots here are two ellipses. The second letter is L, fifty, and doubling it gives C, a hundred.
explanation.definitionFit: During an eclipse the sun's light is blocked, so eclipses are losses of solar power.

clue.text: Upstanding individual, say, person finally settling in LA?

definitions.text: Upstanding individual, say, person finally settling in LA?

indicators.note: standing up in a down entry means the letters read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: one is a single individual

indicators.note: the letters settle inside the two letters of LA

parts.note: taken as written, the two letters of the city's abbreviation
EG, for example, is what say means

indicators.note: only the last letter of the word is used

parts.note: its last letter

explanation.surface: A decent citizen, perhaps someone who has finally made a home in Los Angeles.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition, and LA is used literally as letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An Angeleno is a resident of Los Angeles, a person who has settled in that city.

clue.text: Across Gag? It'll shock the audience

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a gag tied across the mouth stops anyone from talking
second meaning: a remark so startling that the listeners fall silent

explanation.walkthrough: Gag looks like a joke, but it is the cloth that silences someone.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for anything that brings talk to a halt, whether a physical gag or an outrageous remark.

clue.text: "Fine, rain, unsettled?" Presumptuous framing this question providing a hint for 5a 14

definitions.text: this question providing a hint for 5a 14

indicators.note: the bold word goes around the shuffled weather words like a frame

parts.note: a bold person is forward or presumptuous

indicators.note: unsettled weather is changeable, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A weather forecast that cannot decide between fine and rain, framed by a cheeky question.
explanation.walkthrough: Were you born in a field? is said to someone who leaves the door open, which links it to the door riddle.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase completes the rebuke for leaving a door open, so it hints at the door riddle elsewhere in the grid.

clue.text: See 19
In Vegas tops diamonds with spades

definitions.note: American slang: to ice someone is to kill them, as to top them is in Britain

parts.note: ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: In a Las Vegas card game, diamonds combined with spades come out on top.
explanation.walkthrough: Top is British slang for kill, and ice is the American equivalent, hence In Vegas. Diamonds and spades look like card suits but diamonds is jewellery slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice is American slang for murder, matching the British slang top, so in American usage ices means tops.

clue.text: Tracker finally enclosed within half of nuts, causing some pain?

indicators.note: the pieces go inside the jumbled letters
something nuts is crazy, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be scrambled

indicators.note: only the last letter of the word is used

parts.note: its last letter
enc. is the standard abbreviation for enclosed on a letter

explanation.surface: A tracking device ends up lodged inside a crazy person, which is bound to hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: Pain is the French word for bread, so some pain is a loaf.
explanation.definitionFit: A French loaf is a baguette, a quantity of the bread the French call pain.

clue.text: Low playwright has cut the woman up

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading from the bottom
one part is cut away from the playwright

parts.note: Richard Brinsley Sheridan wrote The Rivals and The School for Scandal
she is a pronoun for a woman

explanation.surface: A low moment when a dramatist slashes the female lead's part.
explanation.walkthrough: Sheridan was an Irish-born playwright of the 18th century.
explanation.definitionFit: A nadir is the lowest point, so it serves as a noun meaning a low.

clue.text: Each program's dated cipher keyed in

indicators.note: the symbol is typed into the program, placed inside it

parts.note: an app is a computer program
cipher is an old word for zero, written as a nought

explanation.surface: A computer program has an out-of-date code typed into it.
explanation.walkthrough: Cipher here is its archaic sense of nought, not a code.
explanation.definitionFit: A pop is informal for each, as in tickets at ten pounds a pop, meaning per item.

clue.text: Record kept by female with fine antique pen

indicators.note: the record is held after the female word, as if she keeps it beside her

parts.note: she refers to a female
an EP is an extended-play record
an antique is old

explanation.surface: A woman keeps a vinyl disc along with a fine old fountain pen.
explanation.walkthrough: Pen looks like a writing tool, but it is an enclosure for animals.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheepfold is an enclosure for sheep, and pen is a synonym for such an animal enclosure.

clue.text: Anxious time in English class?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the grammatical ... of a verb, taught in English lessons

explanation.walkthrough: Time in English class looks like a lesson period, but it is the grammar term for verb time.
explanation.definitionFit: Tense describes nervous strain and also names the grammatical marking of past, present or future time.

clue.text: See 18
With new content on counter perhaps, does without zip

indicators.note: running counter means going the opposite way, so the letters are read backwards
without in its old sense of outside, so the deer go around the nothing

parts.note: does are female deer, examples of the animals
zip is slang for nothing, nil

explanation.surface: Someone who has refitted a shop counter, and manages without a zip.
explanation.walkthrough: Does looks like a verb but is the plural of doe.
explanation.definitionFit: Something relined has had a new lining put in, so it has fresh inner material.
